clue.text: Bearing introduction

definitions.meaning: one's bearing is one's outward look or demeanour
a first showing before the public, as when a performer makes a debut

explanation.surface: Reads like a heading on how to carry oneself when first presented to someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: how someone looks or carries themselves, and the act of turning up or being presented for the first time.

clue.text: Bowmen must ignore her curves

indicators.note: ignoring the word her means leaving those letters out of the bowmen

parts.note: archers are men who shoot with bows
taken as written

explanation.surface: Archers are told to pay no attention to some woman's figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcs are segments of curved lines, so the plural noun matches curves.

clue.text: Do well, being head of sales in right environment

indicators.note: the right word forms the surroundings, so the other piece sits within it

parts.note: proper means correct or right

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A salesperson thrives once running the sales team in the right setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'environment' says the S from the head of 'sales' goes inside PROPER.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to thrive or succeed, a verb synonym for doing well.

clue.text: Millions will support goal mankind set protecting island fauna

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so it comes last
the shuffled letters wrap round and shield the island letter
set here means arranged anew, so the letters are put in a fresh order

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A grand conservation scheme: humanity's aims, backed by money, to protect the wildlife of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges the goal and mankind letters into ANMALKINGDO, which 'protecting' wraps round I; in a down clue 'will support' puts M underneath, at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal kingdom is the whole category of animal life, which is what fauna denotes collectively.

clue.text: Patronage given by Australia holding mace, perhaps

indicators.note: the country's letters hold the other piece within them

parts.note: mace is a spice made from nutmeg husks, so it is an example of one

explanation.surface: Sponsorship granted by Australia while it keeps hold of a ceremonial mace.
explanation.walkthrough: Mace looks like the ceremonial staff, but here it is the spice from nutmeg.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the auspices of someone means with their backing or sponsorship, so the word means patronage.

clue.text: Hold onto cold fish

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
the ling is a long-bodied sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep a firm grip on a chilly fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to grip tightly, a verb synonym for holding onto something.

clue.text: Food giving son a turn?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in family trees
a go is a turn in a game

explanation.surface: Asks whether feeding a boy will make him feel queasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' hints at a turned stomach but is a go in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is a starchy foodstuff from palm pith, used in puddings, so it is an example of food.

clue.text: Taking tea, but talking about arch supporter

indicators.note: taking signals that letters are lifted from inside the words that follow
about here means within, so the letters lie inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Someone having tea while chatting about a keen supporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arch supporter' reads like a devoted fan; it is a structural support for an arch.
explanation.definitionFit: An abuttal is the abutting part where a structure meets its support, as an arch meets its pier.

clue.text: Superfluous views will be mistakes

parts.note: over can mean left over, surplus or in excess
sights are things seen, views

explanation.surface: Claims that unnecessary viewpoints will turn out to be errors.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversights are errors made through failure to notice, a plural noun synonym for mistakes.

clue.text: Calls about working for associates

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the calls go round the other piece

parts.note: cries are calls or shouts
on means operating or working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: Phone calls about work made to colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: Cronies are close companions, often with a hint of collusion, so they are associates.

clue.text: Add one new hint about day

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the hint goes round the day letter

parts.note: a clue is a hint

explanation.surface: Instructions to append a fresh tip about the date.
explanation.definitionFit: To include something is to put it in with the rest, a verb synonym for add.

clue.text: Output of broadcaster with some boring link from Europe

parts.note: a television channel is what a broadcaster puts out
a tunnel is the product of a stretch of boring through rock

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that some of a TV station's programmes are dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' suggests dull TV; it means drilling. The Channel Tunnel runs under the English Channel between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: The rail tunnel under the sea is Britain's fixed connection to mainland Europe.

clue.text: Insect making chap at devotions sit back?

parts.note: a chap at his devotions is a man at prayer

indicators.note: back means the word sit is read backwards

explanation.surface: Asks whether a man at prayer should lean back in his seat.
explanation.definitionFit: The praying mantis is a predatory insect named for the folded forelegs it holds as if in prayer.

clue.text: Rolls of fat making spry eaters upset?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Wonders whether nimble diners get annoyed about their paunches.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare tyres is a jocular idiom for rolls of flab round the waist.

clue.text: Cat, say, welcoming a search for a bird

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the pet letters enclose the others

parts.note: a cat is an example of a pet
to rake is to search thoroughly, as in raking through records

explanation.surface: A cat greets someone who is hunting for a bird, which bodes badly for the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A parakeet is a small long-tailed parrot, so it is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Remove blockage and a French swallow returns

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: returns means the swallow word is read backwards

parts.note: a gulp is a swallow

explanation.surface: Clearing a drain, and a French swallow (the bird) comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallow' suggests the migrating bird; it is a gulp.
explanation.definitionFit: To unplug is to take out a stopper or clear an obstruction, which removes a blockage.

clue.text: Industry needing tabloid deal?

parts.note: rag is a disparaging name for a sensational newspaper
to trade is to deal, buy and sell

explanation.surface: A business that relies on cheap newspaper deals.
explanation.definitionFit: The rag trade is an informal name for the clothing business, an industry.

clue.text: Feel bitter about fees regularly being included in lease

indicators.note: these words put the picked letters inside the lease word

parts.note: to rent is to lease

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken from fees

explanation.surface: A tenant is aggrieved at fees built into a lease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks ES, the even letters of 'fees'.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent something is to feel aggrieved or bitter about it, a matching verb.

clue.text: Keeps mum close, and slumps, oddly

parts.note: to shut is to close

indicators.note: oddly means the odd-numbered letters are taken from slumps

explanation.surface: Someone stays quiet near their mother, who slumps strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' seems to be a mother; it means silent. 'oddly' takes S, U, P from 'slumps'.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut up is to fall silent, and keeping mum is the idiom for staying silent.

clue.text: Protection offered by stablemate?

indicators.note: offered by means the letters are provided from within the word that follows

explanation.surface: Asks whether a horse's companion gives cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A table mat shields a table surface from hot dishes, so it is a form of protection.

clue.text: Manages and gets to party

parts.note: to make a place is to reach it, as in making the station in time
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone copes and still reaches the party.
explanation.definitionFit: Makes do is an idiom for coping with what is available, so it means manages.

clue.text: Amazed, seeing small pick-up possibly after crash

indicators.note: after puts the small and pick-up pieces behind the crash piece

parts.note: a crash of thunder; thunder is a crashing noise
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing sizes
a pick-up is a type of truck, so an example of one

explanation.surface: Someone stunned to see a little pick-up truck after a road accident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash' suggests a road accident; it is a peal of thunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Thunderstruck means astounded, as if hit by a sudden shock, so it means amazed.

clue.text: Peak may be cooler with no lid

indicators.note: in a down entry the lid is the top letter, which is removed

parts.note: a fridge keeps food cool

explanation.surface: A summit might be cold enough to count as a refrigerator without a cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long narrow crest of high ground, which can form a peak.

clue.text: Puts a limit on most of room on the way up

indicators.note: in a down entry reading upwards means the letters are reversed
most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: room means space, as in room to move

explanation.surface: Restricting how much of a room is used on the climb upstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims SPACE to SPAC, which 'on the way up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: To cap something is to set a ceiling on it, so caps means puts a limit on.

clue.text: Carried on and stupidly measured missing area

indicators.note: stupidly means done without sense, so the letters are scrambled
missing means the area letter is left out

explanation.surface: Someone continued, having foolishly measured but left out a section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes A from MEASURED; 'stupidly' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Resumed means started again after a pause, so it means carried on.

clue.text: State of mind upsetting men in large part of the world

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the continent

parts.note: Asia is the largest continent

indicators.note: upsetting means overturning, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A frame of mind that unsettles men across a big region.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is loss of memory, a condition of the mind.

clue.text: Call for help about parking concessions

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the distress call goes round the parking letter

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
P is the abbreviation for parking on road signs

explanation.surface: An appeal for assistance with parking allowances.
explanation.definitionFit: Sops are small things given to placate someone, so they are concessions.

clue.text: Revolting acts of rugby team after changing beer line

indicators.note: after puts the team behind the shuffled letters
changing means altering the order of the letters

parts.note: the Lions is the British and Irish touring rugby union side

explanation.surface: Disgusting conduct by a rugby side after they swap the beer line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolting' reads as disgusting; it means rising up. The Lions are the British and Irish rugby union touring team.
explanation.definitionFit: Rebellions are uprisings, and revolting means rising against authority.
